messages.subject: model selection for spatial prediction
parts:
Hi All,

I have a question about model selection. I'm running some distance sampling models using gdistsamp, with the primary objective to make spatial predictions of animal density throughout the study area based on environmental covariates. 

I ran a group of candidate models, and ranked them by AIC. For some of the models, I included detection covariates, and for others I didn't.  My problem is, the top fitting model is composed of a group of abundance covariates and a detection covariate (shrub height). But without the detection covariate, this same group of abundance covariates ranks very poorly.  

My understanding of the predict function to calculate density is that only the covariates that were involved in the lambda formula are used to predict density, is that right? So when I predict density using this model, am I in effect using the poorly fitting model? Should I not try to fit detection covariates when my primary goal is spatial prediction? My models and AIC list are shown below, with the models in question in bold.

Thanks very much for any advice!

Lucretia

model aic delta aic
minshrub 17563.58
climtopog 17581.84 18.26136
clim 17583.69 20.11305
global 17588.19 24.61273
topo 17588.22 24.64629
mintpi 17588.32 24.7447
veg 17589.2 25.62311
minday 17589.69 26.11082
minhshrub 17589.89 26.31491
vegtopo 17590.81 27.23835
min 17625.34 61.76268
vegclim 17626.31 62.73934
soil 17626.46 62.88575
vegsoil 17628.57 64.99645
null 17630.98 67.40814

wtp <- list()

wtp$global <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100+fract_clay+bedrock+
ppt_decjan+ppt_apma+tmin_jan+elev1k+surfar1k+tpi500+road_dist+well_dist,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$topo <- gdistsamp(~elev1k+surfar1k+tpi500,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$clim <- gdistsamp(~ppt_decjan+ppt_apma+tmin_jan,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$veg <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$soil <- gdistsamp(~fract_clay+bedrock,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$min <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$vegtopo <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100+elev1k+surfar1k+tpi500,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)

output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$vegsoil <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100+fract_clay+bedrock,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$mintpi <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~tpi250,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$minhshrub <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~hshrub250,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$minshrub <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~shrub250,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$minday <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~day,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$null <- gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",output="density",unitsOut=("kmsq"),mixture="NB",se=F)

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] model selection for spatial prediction
parts:
Lucretia,
 the predict() function will make predictions of E(N)  which are adjusted for whatever model for encounter probability you used to produce the fit object.   Of if you provide a fitlist, then it should produce model-averaged predictions (i.e., averaged over each of the models for encounter probability, using AIC weights).
regards
andy

parts:
Hi Andy,

Thanks so much for your response. I was basing my understanding of predict from the supplementary R code used in yours and Sillett et al's 2012 Eco Apps paper. They are using gdistsamp as well, and their model has a detection covariate (forest). The code I was looking at says that it's verifying what predict is doing, but it seems to only use the coefficients from the abundance part of the model. Am I misunderstanding their R code? Or are the encounter probabilities already taken into account in the abundance coefficients? I pasted the model and code from their Supplementary material below.

Thanks so much for your help.

spr$C2E2.F_NB <- gdistsamp(~chap + I(chap^2) + elev + I(elev^2), ~1, ~forest,
    umfSpr, mixture="NB", starts=c(1, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 4.6, 0, 0), 
    output="abund", K=200)

## extract the coefficients for the best model
betaspr<-coef(spr$C2E2.F_NB)
betaspr<-betaspr[c("lambda(Int)","lambda(chap)","lambda(elev)","lambda(I(chap^2))","lambda(I(elev^2))")]
beta<-coef(fall$C2E.C_NB)
betafall<-beta[c("lambda(Int)","lambda(chap)","lambda(elev)","lambda(I(chap^2))")]

## use those to verify what predict() is doing. predict is doing exactly this:
Xspr<-cbind(rep(1,307),covs[,1],covs[,2],covs[,1]^2,covs[,2]^2)
pspr<-Xspr%*%(betaspr)
sum(exp(pspr))

parts:
yes it only uses coefficients from the abundance part of the model, but those are estimated jointly with the encounter probability model having whatever effects in it you had specified. So the fitted abundance model is "adjusted" in that sense.
regards
andy

On Tuesday, December 3, 2013 11:53:39 AM UTC-7, Jeffrey Royle wrote:
yes it only uses coefficients from the abundance part of the model, but those are estimated jointly with the encounter probability model having whatever effects in it you had specified. So the fitted abundance model is "adjusted" in that sense.
regards
andy
 


On Tue, Dec 3, 2013 at 1:51 PM, L. Olson <lucre...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Andy,

Thanks so much for your response. I was basing my understanding of predict from the supplementary R code used in yours and Sillett et al's 2012 Eco Apps paper. They are using gdistsamp as well, and their model has a detection covariate (forest). The code I was looking at says that it's verifying what predict is doing, but it seems to only use the coefficients from the abundance part of the model. Am I misunderstanding their R code? Or are the encounter probabilities already taken into account in the abundance coefficients? I pasted the model and code from their Supplementary material below.

Thanks so much for your help.

spr$C2E2.F_NB <- gdistsamp(~chap + I(chap^2) + elev + I(elev^2), ~1, ~forest,
    umfSpr, mixture="NB", starts=c(1, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 4.6, 0, 0), 
    output="abund", K=200)

## extract the coefficients for the best model
betaspr<-coef(spr$C2E2.F_NB)
betaspr<-betaspr[c("lambda(Int)","lambda(chap)","lambda(elev)","lambda(I(chap^2))","lambda(I(elev^2))")]
beta<-coef(fall$C2E.C_NB)
betafall<-beta[c("lambda(Int)","lambda(chap)","lambda(elev)","lambda(I(chap^2))")]

## use those to verify what predict() is doing. predict is doing exactly this:
Xspr<-cbind(rep(1,307),covs[,1],covs[,2],covs[,1]^2,covs[,2]^2)
pspr<-Xspr%*%(betaspr)
sum(exp(pspr))




On Tuesday, December 3, 2013 11:35:34 AM UTC-7, Jeffrey Royle wrote:
Lucretia,
 the predict() function will make predictions of E(N)  which are adjusted for whatever model for encounter probability you used to produce the fit object.   Of if you provide a fitlist, then it should produce model-averaged predictions (i.e., averaged over each of the models for encounter probability, using AIC weights).
regards
andy
 
 


On Tue, Dec 3, 2013 at 1:27 PM, L. Olson <lucre...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi All,

I have a question about model selection. I'm running some distance sampling models using gdistsamp, with the primary objective to make spatial predictions of animal density throughout the study area based on environmental covariates. 

I ran a group of candidate models, and ranked them by AIC. For some of the models, I included detection covariates, and for others I didn't.  My problem is, the top fitting model is composed of a group of abundance covariates and a detection covariate (shrub height). But without the detection covariate, this same group of abundance covariates ranks very poorly.  

My understanding of the predict function to calculate density is that only the covariates that were involved in the lambda formula are used to predict density, is that right? So when I predict density using this model, am I in effect using the poorly fitting model? Should I not try to fit detection covariates when my primary goal is spatial prediction? My models and AIC list are shown below, with the models in question in bold.

Thanks very much for any advice!

Lucretia

model aic delta aic
minshrub 17563.58
climtopog 17581.84 18.26136
clim 17583.69 20.11305
global 17588.19 24.61273
topo 17588.22 24.64629
mintpi 17588.32 24.7447
veg 17589.2 25.62311
minday 17589.69 26.11082
minhshrub 17589.89 26.31491
vegtopo 17590.81 27.23835
min 17625.34 61.76268
vegclim 17626.31 62.73934
soil 17626.46 62.88575
vegsoil 17628.57 64.99645
null 17630.98 67.40814

wtp <- list()

wtp$global <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100+fract_clay+bedrock+
ppt_decjan+ppt_apma+tmin_jan+elev1k+surfar1k+tpi500+road_dist+well_dist,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$topo <- gdistsamp(~elev1k+surfar1k+tpi500,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$clim <- gdistsamp(~ppt_decjan+ppt_apma+tmin_jan,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$veg <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$soil <- gdistsamp(~fract_clay+bedrock,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$min <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$vegtopo <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100+elev1k+surfar1k+tpi500,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$vegclim <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100+ppt_decjan+ppt_apma+tmin_jan,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$climtopog <- gdistsamp(~ppt_decjan+ppt_apma+tmin_jan+elev1k+surfar1k+tpi500,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$vegsoil <- gdistsamp(~bare100+h_shrub100+sage100+fract_clay+bedrock,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$mintpi <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~tpi250,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$minhshrub <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~hshrub250,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$minshrub <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~shrub250,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$minday <- gdistsamp(~bare100+fract_clay+ppt_apma+elev1k+road_dist,~1,~day,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)
wtp$null <- gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1,wtp.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",output="density",unitsOut=("kmsq"),mixture="NB",se=F)

parts:
Lucrecia, 
If you compare the coefficient values estimated from the top-fitting model (with detection covariate) with the coefficient values estimated from its poorly-fitting twin (without the detection covariate), they will not be the same (and neither will the densities estimated from the two models). The detection covariate influences the estimation of coefficient values on the abundance covariates, but only the abundance covariates are then used to estimate density. 

- Phil
